Name: RT-LIM-16 Save Group autocomplete populated from stats table limit names
Objective: Verify that the Limit cell autocomplete in the Save Group dialog suggests only names that are present in the current stats table after Parse/Write Statistic has run.
Precondition: ST-09 passed. Stats table contains at least two distinct limitName values. Save Group dialog is open (ST-16 precondition met).
Test Script (Step): Click on the Limit cell of any row in the Save Group dialog Limits table and start typing the first letter of a known limit name.
Test Script (Test Data): First letter of a known limit name from the stats table
Test Script (Expected Result): An autocomplete dropdown appears listing limit names that begin with the typed letter. All suggestions correspond to names visible in the stats table limitName column.

Test Script (Step): Clear the cell and type a prefix that does not match any limit name.
Test Script (Test Data): A string not matching any limit name
Test Script (Expected Result): Autocomplete dropdown is empty or absent. No phantom suggestions appear. Application does not crash.

Name: RT-LIM-17 Load Input Config File cancel leaves path label unchanged
Objective: Verify that opening the Load Input Config File dialog and clicking Cancel does not change the stats input config path label.
Precondition: Application launched. The stats input config path label shows config/StatisticsLimitsConfig.json.
Test Script (Step): Note the current path shown in the stats input config path label.
Test Script (Expected Result): Path label shows config/StatisticsLimitsConfig.json.

Test Script (Step): Click the Load Input Config File button. When the file dialog opens click Cancel.
Test Script (Expected Result): File dialog closes immediately. The stats input config path label still shows config/StatisticsLimitsConfig.json unchanged. No error in the log.

Name: RT-LIM-18 Write Statistic after reloading a different limits file updates the stats table
Objective: Verify that replacing the limits file path and re-running Write Statistic refreshes the stats table with the new limit definitions.
Precondition: ST-09 passed (table populated with limits from BurnInLimits.yaml). A second BurnIn limits YAML with a different set of limitName entries is available.
Test Script (Step): Note the limit names currently shown in the stats table.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table shows limit names from the original BurnInLimits.yaml.

Test Script (Step): On the Parse tab click Load Input Limits File and select the second limits YAML.
Test Script (Expected Result): BurnIn Limits path label updates to the second file path.

Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab and click Write Statistic.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table clears and repopulates with the limit names from the second YAML file. Limit names from the original file that do not appear in the second file are no longer shown. No crash.

Name: RT-LIM-19 Save Group to file on read-only YAML logs error and does not crash
Objective: Verify that attempting to save a group to a read-only groups YAML file logs an appropriate error and does not crash the application.
Precondition: ST-09 passed. config/BurnInLimGroups.yaml is temporarily made read-only (remove write permission). Save Group dialog is open.
Test Script (Step): In the Save Group dialog type a valid group name and add a limit entry. Check Save to file.
Test Script (Test Data): A valid group name; read-only config/BurnInLimGroups.yaml
Test Script (Expected Result): Group Name and Limit cells are filled. Save to file checkbox is checked.

Test Script (Step): Click Save.
Test Script (Expected Result): The dialog closes OR remains open with an error label. An ERROR-level entry appears in the log table describing the file write failure. The application does not crash. Restore write permission to config/BurnInLimGroups.yaml after the test.

Name: RT-LIM-20 Navigating to a newly saved group via forward button works immediately after saving
Objective: Verify that after successfully saving a new group (ST-17) it is immediately reachable by pressing Group > without requiring a restart or re-parse.
Precondition: ST-17 passed. SmokeTestGroup has been saved and confirmed in the combobox.
Test Script (Step): Note the total number of groups shown in the BurnIn combobox.
Test Script (Expected Result): Group count is recorded. SmokeTestGroup is in the list.

Test Script (Step): Click Group > repeatedly until SmokeTestGroup is the active group as shown in the group name label.
Test Script (Expected Result): Each Group > click advances one group. The navigation reaches SmokeTestGroup. Stats table updates to show only the limits matched by the group definition. No crash.

Test Script (Step): Click Group > once more past SmokeTestGroup.
Test Script (Expected Result): Navigation advances to the next group OR wraps to the first group. It does not get stuck on SmokeTestGroup.

Name: RT-LIM-21 Switching BurnIn/Cal radio resets active group index to the first group
Objective: Verify that clicking the opposite radio button (BurnIn to Calibration or vice versa) resets the active group index to 0 so the first group of the new type is shown.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated with both BurnIn and Calibration data. Both comboboxes have at least two entries. Currently on BurnIn radio with group index advanced to index >= 1 by Forward navigation.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Select BurnIn radio. Use Group > to navigate to group index 1 or later. Note the group name label.
Test Script (Expected Result): Group name label shows a BurnIn group other than the first.

Test Script (Step): Click the Calibration radio button.
Test Script (Expected Result): Groups combobox switches to Calibration entries. Group name label shows the first Calibration group (index 0). Stats table updates for the first Calibration group. No error in log.

Test Script (Step): Click the BurnIn radio button.
Test Script (Expected Result): Groups combobox switches back to BurnIn entries. Group name label shows the first BurnIn group (index 0) not the previously active index-1 group. Application does not crash.

Name: RT-LIM-22 Plot cursor tooltip shows correct protocol file name on data point hover
Objective: Verify that hovering over a data point in the stats plot frame triggers the mplcursors tooltip and calls the cursor-select callback with the correct protocol file name.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated. At least one row has Graph = On. The plot frame shows a data series with at least one data point.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Confirm at least one series is plotted.
Test Script (Expected Result): Plot frame shows at least one data series with visible data points.

Test Script (Step): Hover the mouse cursor over any data point in the plot frame and wait for the tooltip.
Test Script (Expected Result): A tooltip (mplcursors annotation) appears near the data point. The tooltip is non-empty and does not raise an exception in the log. The protocol name or x/y values are shown.

Test Script (Step): Click the data point.
Test Script (Expected Result): The cursor-select callback fires. A log entry or any on-screen update (e.g. status label or highlighted row) reflects the selected protocol. No crash.

Name: RT-LIM-23 Stats table x-axis tick spacing adjusts for more than 50 protocols
Objective: Verify that when more than 50 protocols are parsed and plotted the stats plot x-axis does not render one tick per protocol but uses automatic or coarser spacing.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated with more than 50 accepted protocols. At least one limit row has Graph = On.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Set Graph = On for a limit row and confirm the plot renders.
Test Script (Expected Result): Plot frame shows a series across more than 50 x-axis points.

Test Script (Step): Inspect the x-axis tick marks in the plot frame.
Test Script (Expected Result): The x-axis does NOT show 50+ individual tick labels. Matplotlib automatic tick spacing is applied. The axis remains legible. No crash.

Name: RT-LIM-24 Export .pptx with multiple On-series creates correct number of slides
Objective: Verify that exporting to pptx with N series enabled (Graph = On) creates at least N slides and that no series is silently omitted.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated. Three distinct limit rows have Graph = On. output/ is writable.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Confirm exactly three rows show Graph = On.
Test Script (Expected Result): Three rows: Graph = On.

Test Script (Step): Note any existing .pptx files in output/.
Test Script (Expected Result): Baseline file list recorded.

Test Script (Step): Click Export .pptx. Wait for completion.
Test Script (Expected Result): New .pptx file appears in output/. No ERROR-level log entry.

Test Script (Step): Open the .pptx file and count the slides that contain data charts.
Test Script (Expected Result): The file contains at least 3 data slides (one per On-series or one per exported chart type). No slide is completely blank. No series data is missing.

Name: RT-LIM-25 Re-parse after Clear Data re-enables groups combobox and fills it
Objective: Verify that after calling Clear Data from the Parse tab and re-importing and re-parsing protocols the Statistics tab group comboboxes are repopulated and functional again.
Precondition: Application in a freshly started state. Protocol files and limits/groups YAMLs are available.
Test Script (Step): Parse a set of protocols with BurnIn and Cal limits loaded. Confirm the Statistics tab shows group entries.
Test Script (Test Data): BurnIn and Cal protocol files; BurnInLimits.yaml; CalLimits.yaml
Test Script (Expected Result): Groups comboboxes are populated. Statistics tab works normally.

Test Script (Step): Switch to the Parse tab. Click Clear Data.
Test Script (Expected Result): Status label reads No protocols loaded. Groups comboboxes become empty/disabled. Stats table clears. No crash.

Test Script (Step): Re-import the same protocol files and click Parse Data. Then click Write Statistic.
Test Script (Expected Result): Parsing completes. Statistics tab groups comboboxes are re-enabled and contain the same group entries as before the clear. Stats table is populated. No crash.

Name: RT-LIM-26 Save Group dialog Add Line keeps autocomplete functional in new rows
Objective: Verify that rows added by the Add Line button in the Save Group dialog support the same limit-name autocomplete as the pre-existing rows.
Precondition: ST-18 passed. Save Group dialog is open and Add Line has been clicked to create at least one extra row.
Test Script (Step): Click the Limit cell of a row added by Add Line (last row in the table).
Test Script (Expected Result): Limit cell is editable.

Test Script (Step): Start typing the first letter of a known limit name.
Test Script (Test Data): First letter of a limit name from the stats table
Test Script (Expected Result): Autocomplete dropdown appears with matching limit names identical to the suggestions available in the original rows. Application does not crash.

Name: RT-LIM-27 Contains match is case-insensitive for limit name filtering
Objective: Verify that a Contains match group filters limits regardless of the case of the typed substring.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated with limit names that share a common root word but differ in capitalisation e.g. Power_RX and POWER_TX. A Contains group CaseGroup is set up with substring power.
Test Script (Step): Navigate to the Contains group CaseGroup via the Forward button.
Test Script (Expected Result): Group name label shows BurnIn: CaseGroup or Calibration: CaseGroup.

Test Script (Step): Inspect the stats table rows.
Test Script (Expected Result): All limit rows whose name contains power or Power or POWER (case-insensitive) are shown. No matching row is excluded due to case difference. Application does not crash.

Name: RT-LIM-28 Graph color assignment is stable across Add/Remove series toggling
Objective: Verify that toggling Graph Off and then On for a row re-assigns the same color as the first assignment and does not cycle to a different color each time.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated. Row 0 has Graph = On. The color of the row-0 series is noted from the plot legend e.g. blue.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Confirm row 0 Graph = On. Note the legend label color for that series.
Test Script (Expected Result): Row 0 series is drawn in the expected color (index 0 = blue).

Test Script (Step): Click the Graph cell of row 0 to toggle it to Off. Confirm the series disappears from the plot.
Test Script (Expected Result): Series is removed from the plot. Legend no longer shows that entry.

Test Script (Step): Click the Graph cell of row 0 again to toggle it back to On.
Test Script (Expected Result): Series re-appears in the plot. The color is the same as the first time (blue / index 0). The legend label is not a different color. No duplicate legend entry appears. No crash.
